children.title: Abstract
children.body: We explicitly rewrite the path integral for the free or critical (or ) bosonic vector models in space-time dimensions as a path integral over fields (including massless high-spin fields) living on ()-dimensional anti-de Sitter space. Inspired by de Mello Koch, Jevicki, Suzuki and Yoon and earlier work, we first rewrite the vector models in terms of bi-local fields, then expand these fields in eigenmodes of the conformal group, and finally map these eigenmodes to those of fields on anti-de Sitter space. Our results provide an explicit (non-local) action for a high-spin theory on anti-de Sitter space, which is presumably equivalent in the large limit to Vasiliev’s classical high-spin gravity theory (with some specific gauge-fixing to a fixed background), but which can be used also for loop computations. Our mapping is explicit within the expansion, but in principle can be extended also to finite theories, where extra constraints on products of bulk fields need to be taken into account.

The AdS/CFT correspondence [1, 2, 3] is a general relation between conformal field theories (CFTs) in space-time dimensions and quantum gravity theories on -dimensional asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) space-times. For the quantum gravity theories do not have any independent non-perturbative definition, so the correspondence should be viewed as defining them in terms of the corresponding CFT. When the CFT has an appropriate large limit, its expansion may be identified with a perturbative expansion of the bulk theory, such that this theory is classical in the large limit. One can then check the correspondence by comparing this perturbative expansion of the bulk theory (which is well-defined, for instance, if the bulk is a superstring theory) with the expansion of the CFT. This perturbative expansion starts with some classical solution of the bulk theory (this can be a solution of string theory, or, in an appropriate limit, a solution of its supergravity approximation) and quantizes the theory around it. Many checks of the correspondence have been done within this expansion (see, for instance, [4, 5, 6]), and in special cases it has even been proven to all orders in this expansion [7, 8, 9].

gist.html: AdS/CFT is tested within the $1/N$ expansion, where the bulk is a classical solution quantized perturbatively.

children.body: Beyond perturbation theory in , the bulk theory is implicitly defined by the CFT, but it would be nice to understand what this definition means for the bulk fields. Is there still for finite any description of the theory as a sum over bulk gravity configurations, or is the gravity description an effective description that is only valid within the context of the expansion? Do off-shell gravitational configurations have any meaning? Even in the semi-classical limit, it is not clear if we need to sum over all possible gravitational solutions with appropriate boundary conditions, or if there are some limitations. This question arises, for instance, when considering a CFT on a disconnected space-time, where in some cases gravitational solutions connecting two components of the space-time through the bulk exist, but including them in the partition function would contradict locality in the CFT; in the case such configurations are included on the (well-defined) gravity side, related to the fact that the dual CFT is an ensemble of theories rather than a specific CFT [10, 11], but the situation in higher dimensions is not clear.

gist.html: Beyond $1/N$ the CFT defines the bulk only implicitly: is it still a sum over bulk configurations, and which?

children.body: In this paper we would like to suggest answers to these questions, in the context of one of the simplest examples of the AdS/CFT correspondence, the duality between bosonic vector models (with ) and high-spin gravity theories [12]. The CFT in this case is just the theory of complex scalar fields (), with a projection to -invariant states and operators (alternatively one can consider real scalar fields and project to invariants). In general it is subtle to impose this projection while keeping the CFT local (though for this can be done by coupling to a Chern-Simons theory at infinite level [13, 14, 15]), but in this paper we focus just on correlation functions in flat space, where this subtlety does not arise. We will map the -singlet sector of these CFTs to bulk fields (with all integer spins) living on a fixed AdS space, obtaining a description of the theory as a path integral over these bulk fields. Within the expansion we will write down an explicit (albeit non-local) action for the bulk theory, and we will argue that it allows for perturbative computations, with all loop divergences canceling when appropriate counter-terms (which we write down explicitly) are introduced. For finite we will argue that the theory can still be written as a path integral over the same bulk fields, but that these fields obey complicated non-local constraints involving products of bulk fields, such that most configurations of the bulk fields are not included in the path integral (indeed, even anti-de Sitter space itself turns out not to be one of the allowed bulk configurations for finite ). Interestingly, we do not see any sign of a sum over different topologies in the bulk, but only of continuous field configurations (including fluctuations of the metric) on a fixed anti-de Sitter space.

gist.html: For vector models, singlets map to all-spin fields on fixed AdS; finite $N$ adds constraints, and no topology sum appears.

children.title: Vector models and high-spin gravity
children.body: A vector model of $N$ free scalars, restricted to $U(N)$ or $O(N)$ singlets, has single-trace operators $\phi^*\partial^J\phi$ of every spin $J$, and for $J\ge1$ they are conserved currents of dimension $d-2+J$. In AdS/CFT a conserved current of spin $J$ is dual to a massless gauge field of spin $J$, as the stress tensor is dual to the graviton. The bulk dual must therefore contain massless fields of all spins: a high-spin gravity, weakly coupled when $N$ is large, with $1/N$ playing the role of Newton's constant. Klebanov and Polyakov conjectured such a duality for the critical $O(N)$ model, and the free model is its simplest case. Vasiliev constructed consistent classical equations of motion for interacting massless fields of all spins in AdS, with an infinite-dimensional gauge symmetry, but no action principle is known for them, so neither loop corrections nor the relative weight of different solutions can be computed. The paper builds the bulk theory from the CFT side instead.

We focus on studying this case of free CFTs (and their deformations) since it is the simplest case on the field theory side, where we can easily perform explicit computations. In this case the dual gravitational theories are only understood classically, where they are believed to be described by the equations of motion of Vasiliev’s high-spin gravity [16, 17, 18]. No action is known for these theories,1 which would allow one to compare the partition functions of different solutions, or to compute loop corrections by summing over off-shell modes. Thus, an additional motivation to study this case is that our formalism provides a bulk action for these gravitational theories that allows these computations to be performed, and thus constructs a quantum completion for high-spin gravity theories. Vasiliev’s equations have a huge gauge symmetry, while our bulk fields live on a fixed anti-de Sitter space and have no gauge redundancy. We show that the physical degrees of freedom following from our action match those of Vasiliev’s high-spin gravity. We believe, though we have not shown this, that there is a specific gauge-fixing of Vasiliev’s equations which will reduce them to the classical equations of motion that follow from our bulk action. Note that the huge gauge symmetry of Vasiliev’s equations allows them to be written in a formalism which has a fixed background metric [25], as we have.

gist.html: Vasiliev's high-spin gravity has no action; this one supplies it, with matching degrees of freedom, presumably in a gauge.

children.body:
The formalism we use to construct the bulk theory is based on the idea of bi-local holography [26, 27, 28, 29, 30], and in particular inspired by the recent paper [31]. We begin in section 2 by changing variables in our CFT path integral from the fundamental fields to the bi-local -invariant fields

(1.1)

Correlation functions of these fields capture all the -invariant information of the theory, so that we do not lose any information (or any -invariant deformations) by changing to these variables. Performing this change of variables requires introducing a cutoff in the field theory, which can be thought of as having a finite number of space-time points. In the large limit we can perform the change of variables explicitly, and most of our paper will focus on this limit and on the resulting expansion. For finite in the continuum limit, the change of variables can still be performed but the bi-local variables obey complicated constraints, that will map in our formalism to complicated constraints on the bulk fields.

gist.html: First step: change variables to the bi-local $G(x_1,x_2)$, explicit when $N$ exceeds the number of lattice points.

In order to map the bi-local fields to the bulk, we first expand them in a basis of eigen-modes of the conformal group (we work in Euclidean space throughout this paper for simplicity), given by three-point functions (where the first two operators are scalar operators with the free field dimension , and the last one has dimension and spin ) [32, 33]. This is the topic of section 3, where we rewrite our CFT action in variables which are the coefficients of these eigen-modes. In section 4 we show (see also [31]) that modes with precisely the same quantum numbers arise when considering symmetric traceless transverse fields of spin in , with all non-negative-integer spins . In this case the eigen-modes are bulk-to-boundary propagators [34], connecting a point in the bulk of AdS space with a point on its boundary. It is then natural to identify the coefficients of the eigen-modes in the CFT with the coefficients of the bulk fields, up to a possible constant (which can depend on the mode). This gives us an explicit linear mapping between the fluctuation around the bi-local field (1.1) and the bulk fields :2

We can then use this map to write down the bulk action for the higher spin fields, which turns out to be explicitly non-local. In section 5 we show that for a specific choice of the constant in the mapping we can obtain a local quadratic term in the bulk action, albeit one that is quartic in derivatives, of the schematic form

(1.3)

where . Quantizing this action leads to two particles of each spin in the bulk. One of these has a positive propagator and matches with the expected physical particles in the bulk theory (including massless high-spin particles, that are dual to the conserved currents with of the free CFT). The other has a negative propagator, and we interpret it as an unphysical ‘ghost’ mode (in some cases we can show that the quantum numbers of these ‘ghosts’ match with the ones arising from a specific gauge-fixing of Vasiliev’s equations of motion).

gist.html: One choice of $f_{\Delta,J}$ gives a local four-derivative quadratic action: a physical particle and a ghost per spin.

children.body: In section 6 we discuss the Feynman rules for performing computations with our bulk action, and argue that all loop divergences cancel so that we can perform computations to all orders in . In principle this is automatic in our formalism since we directly map the field theory to the bulk, so we are guaranteed to get finite results to all orders in which agree with the CFT, but one has to be careful about several regularizations that are needed in order to get sensible results.

gist.html: Bulk Feynman rules with counter-terms are argued to cancel all loop divergences, giving finite results at every order.

children.body: In the final two sections we apply our formalism to two interesting deformations of the CFT. In section 7 we discuss a mass deformation where we give a mass to the fields , such that the field theory is still free but is no longer conformal. We show that in our formalism there is a corresponding classical solution of the bulk equations of motion, with the appropriate boundary condition. This solution still lives on anti-de Sitter space, but there is a scalar field turned on which breaks the isometries of AdS. In section 8 we discuss the deformation of the free theory to the critical theory, which is a non-trivial interacting CFT. As expected [36, 37], the critical theory is described by the same bulk action but with a different boundary condition for the bulk scalar field, which leads to non-trivial (but finite) loop corrections.

gist.html: A mass gives a bulk scalar breaking AdS isometries; the critical theory changes only the scalar's boundary condition.

children.body: Several appendices contain some technical results.
There are many remaining open questions and future directions, and we list some of them here.

A very intriguing question is whether our main result, that we can rewrite our CFT as a bulk path integral over fields living on a fixed anti-de Sitter background, generalizes to more complicated theories. We derived this result for vector models on , and it seems likely that even for these theories on more complicated backgrounds, such as backgrounds including circles, this will need to be modified (for instance, the vector models on a circle exhibit phase transitions in the large limit [38], which are expected to map to transitions between different topologies in the bulk). Putting the vector models on more complicated backgrounds requires adding (or ) gauge fields (in particular holonomies around circles), and it would be interesting to understand if this can be done in our framework. Generalizing our framework to matrix models (such as one would get, in particular, in the presence of dynamical gauge fields) seems very complicated, due to the large number of independent invariants that exist in this case (beyond the bi-local fields (1.1)). However, perhaps some general lessons may still apply also in that case.

gist.html: Whether a fixed-AdS path integral survives on backgrounds with circles, or for matrix models, is open.

children.body:
Some more specific questions are :

  • It would be nice to prove that in the classical limit our bulk theories are identical to Vasiliev’s high-spin gravity theories in some gauge; we expect this to be the case since these theories are claimed to be unique.

  • It would be interesting to understand the relation between our approach and earlier approaches to derive the AdS/CFT correspondence in this case of free vector models, such as approaches based on identifying the radial direction with a renormalization group scale [39, 40, 41, 42].

  • The action we obtain on anti-de Sitter space is manifestly non-local. On general grounds we do not expect the gravitational dual to free field theories to be local at distances shorter than the anti-de Sitter radius, but we do expect it to be local at much longer distance scales. It would be nice to confirm that the actions that we obtain have this property.

  • In our approach we do not directly use the high-spin symmetry of the free field theories, partly because we are interested in applications like the finite critical models where it is broken. The presence of massless high-spin fields in the bulk implies that our bulk theory is a gauge-fixed version of a theory in which this high-spin symmetry is gauged. It would be interesting to understand the implementation of this symmetry in our formalism and whether it can be made more explicit.

  • It would be interesting to understand better the constraints on our bulk fields at finite , and whether there is a nice way to write these constraints in the bulk language. More speculatively, non-local relations between quantum gravity fields (which we find) may be related to the black hole information paradox.

  • In this paper we analyzed only two solutions of the classical bulk theory (dual to the large CFT), corresponding to the undeformed CFT and to its mass deformation. It would be interesting to study other solutions.

  • It is natural to generalize our analysis to have fermions instead of scalars, and work on this is in progress [43]. One advantage of using fermions is that (unlike free scalars) they are primary fields also for , so one can include this case in the analysis. Another generalization, to the singlet sector of flavors of scalars (each with components), is straightforward, and just requires replacing our bulk fields by matrices (with the bulk action involving a single trace over products of these fields). It is also interesting to generalize our results to theories having both fermions and scalars, and, in particular, to supersymmetric vector models.

  • In this paper we focus on , but our methods can be used (with some modifications) also for the case of conformal quantum mechanics. In this case it would be interesting to relate our results to many results on the SYK model (see [44] for a review), which can also be written in bi-local variables that are mapped to the bulk [45], and to various recent results on gravitational theories on .

  • It would be interesting to analyze vector models on other space-times. In particular, the theory on is related by a conformal transformation to the theory on , so it should be easy to generalize our analysis to this case, and to perform a bulk computation of the partition function of these theories. Attempts to do this in high-spin gravity at one-loop order appeared in [46, 47, 48]; our framework will allow us to compute also the leading order partition function (without which the one-loop result is not really meaningful), and it will lead to a different one-loop result than the one in [46, 47, 48] (because we have different quadratic terms in the bulk).

  • It would be interesting to generalize our analysis to (or ) gauge theories, instead of (). The big difference in this case is the appearance of extra baryon-like operators, where fields are contracted with an epsilon symbol, and it would be interesting to understand how to take these operators into account in our framework.

  • In the case, a natural generalization of our models is by coupling them to a Chern-Simons theory, as this does not add any new dynamical fields. The resulting theories still have a high-spin symmetry in the large limit (with fixed ‘t Hooft coupling ), though the symmetry is broken at finite , and in the large limit the dual gravitational theory is believed to be a continuous deformation of the Vasiliev high-spin gravity theories by turning on a single extra coupling there, related to the ‘t Hooft coupling [14, 15]. In our framework the modification seems to be much more drastic, since the bi-locals (1.1) are no longer gauge-invariant (they can be made gauge-invariant by inserting a Wilson line connecting and ), but the results on the classical gravity dual at infinite suggest that at least within the expansion there should be a simple way to implement this generalization.

  • It would be interesting to generalize our analysis to Lorentzian space, and to understand how the Wick rotation affects our mappings and the bulk physics.4 In particular it would be nice to understand the Hilbert space in the bulk, and the role of the “ghost”-like fields. It would also be interesting to look for Lorentzian classical solutions corresponding to finite energy density states of the CFT, which we expect to map to black holes on the gravity side, though the free theory does not thermalize so the dynamics of these black holes is quite different from standard ones.

  • Some other Euclidean vector models are believed to be dual to gravitational theories on de Sitter space [49], and it would also be interesting to generalize our analysis to these theories, and see if they shed any light on these mysterious gravitational theories.

gist.html: Lists specific open problems, from Vasiliev's gauge and bulk locality to fermions, $S^d$, Chern–Simons couplings and de Sitter.
Open: other backgrounds and matrix models, Vasiliev's gauge, long-distance locality, finite-$N$ constraints, other matter, Lorentzian signature.

brief.html: The main open question is whether a path integral over fields on one fixed AdS survives for other theories and backgrounds. On circles, vector models have phase transitions that are expected to change the bulk topology. More specific questions: is the classical theory Vasiliev's in some gauge, is it local beyond the AdS radius, and how do the finite-$N$ constraints read in the bulk? Extensions to fermions, $S^d$, $SU(N)$, Chern–Simons couplings, Lorentzian signature and de Sitter space are listed too.

gist.html: Vector models are rewritten as a high-spin theory on fixed AdS, with an explicit action that also computes loops.

brief.html: Beyond the $1/N$ expansion the CFT defines its gravity dual only implicitly, and it is unclear whether that bulk is still a sum over configurations. For vector models, rewriting the singlet sector through bi-local fields gives a path integral over fields of all spins on one fixed AdS, with no sign of a sum over topologies. Matching conformal eigenmodes to bulk-to-boundary modes gives the map, and one choice of normalization makes the quadratic action local, with a physical field and a ghost for each spin. Loops are argued to cancel with explicit counter-terms, and the mass and critical deformations are mapped too.

children.title: Massless high-spin fields, gauge fixing and ghosts
children.body: A massless high-spin field of spin $J$ is described, following Fronsdal, by a symmetric tensor $\Phi_{\mu_1\dots\mu_J}$ with vanishing double trace and a gauge symmetry $\delta\Phi=\nabla_{(\mu_1}\xi_{\mu_2\dots\mu_J)}$ whose parameter is a traceless tensor of spin $J-1$, generalizing the photon and the graviton. Gauge fixing to a transverse traceless field, like the Lorenz or de Donder gauge, leaves only the physical polarizations, but the Faddeev–Popov determinant then contributes a ghost field of spin $J-1$ with a definite mass. In AdS a massless spin-$J$ field is dual to a conserved current of dimension $d-2+J$, and its ghost has spin $J-1$ and dimension $d+J-1$, the quantum numbers of the current's divergence. In one-loop computations the ghosts remove the unphysical gauge modes. The paper's wrong-sign modes, of spin $J'$ and dimension $d+J'$, have exactly these ghost quantum numbers with $J'=J-1$.

For the local choice of , we found that our bulk propagator is the difference of two propagators of on-shell symmetric traceless transverse spin fields, a field with positive propagator and mass , and a field with negative propagator and mass . We identify the on-shell fields of the first type with the physical operators in our theory; note that for these are massless spin fields in the bulk, dual to conserved currents (and, in particular, for we obtain the standard physical part of the propagator for a graviton in a fixed AdS space-time). The particle spectrum that we find, in the case, is exactly the same as the particle spectrum of Vasiliev’s theory, including massless spin fields with all . The canonical quadratic action for such a massless spin field (which is symmetric and double-traceless, see [57, 58, 59]), has (for ) a gauge freedom, which we can gauge-fix to obtain a symmetric traceless transverse field (the details of this gauge-fixing may be found in [57, 58, 59]), and in this gauge we obtain precisely the spin fields that we found in our theory (with the same propagator as for our physical particles, up to a constant). The gauge-fixing leads to an extra ghost field in the bulk, coming from the Faddeev-Popov determinant, with spin and mass , so we can identify the extra negative-propagator modes that we found above with these ghosts (see [60] and references therein). More precisely, for , the original spin field contains also a trace part which is a symmetric spin field, but on-shell one can use extra gauge transformations to set this trace part to zero, consistent with the fact that we do not see the corresponding on-shell modes in our approach; moreover, this extra gauge-fixing precisely makes the ghosts into symmetric traceless transverse tensors, which is what we obtain in our formalism.

gist.html: For $U(N)$ the physical fields are Vasiliev's, and the wrong-sign ones carry Faddeev–Popov ghost quantum numbers.

children.body: While this identification with the expectations from Vasiliev’s theory works very nicely for the case, it actually fails for the case. This is because in our spectrum we find physical and unphysical fields just for even spins, while from the minimal Vasiliev action that would start from massless gauge fields with even spins , we would get physical fields of even spin but unphysical “ghosts” with odd spin. It would be interesting to understand the reason for this discrepancy. In any case, our bulk action by construction provides a consistent dual for the and theories, whether or not it is related to the standard Vasiliev theory in a simple way.

gist.html: For $O(N)$ these ghosts have even spin where Vasiliev's would be odd: an unexplained mismatch.

children.body: Note that even though on-shell we found (for ) precisely the same spectrum as in Vasiliev’s theory, the quadratic terms we find are very different from the naive quadratic terms one would associate with the fields of that theory. Of course in any case Vasiliev’s theory is only known classically (on-shell), so we claim that our action is the correct way to define it off-shell (in perturbation theory in ), in the specific gauge-choice described above (more precisely, we should probably work with the formalism where this theory is written on a fixed AdS background, as in [25]). In our off-shell formulation, our analysis guarantees that at all loop orders this theory (with the specific counter-terms we found) will give the correlation functions of the free theory. Note that, as discussed above, for finite the bulk fields that we find obey complicated constraints, such that even empty AdS space () is not a consistent configuration in the finite path integral; but at any order in we can ignore this.

children.body: In this section we discuss the deformation of the free scalar CFT by a term, which in the bi-local theory is a double-trace deformation , and the critical theory that it leads to in the low-energy () limit for . We start by reviewing the double-trace deformation of the free or CFT, following [64, 65, 66, 67]. We will then discuss the bulk dual of the critical theory, using the off-shell mapping of to the boundary limit of (4.45). We will show how the bulk duals of the free and critical theory only differ by the boundary conditions of the bulk scalar two-point function, as anticipated in [36, 68, 37]. gist.html:
• Context What bulk does a CFT define beyond $1/N$? Simplest case: vector models, dual to high-spin gravity.
  • Result
    • Matching conformal eigenmodes of $\phi^*(x_1)\phi(x_2)$ with AdS modes gives a path integral over all-spin AdS fields.
    • The non-local bulk action is presumably Vasiliev's classical theory, gauge-fixed; its quadratic part can be made local, with Vasiliev's $U(N)$ spectrum.
    • Loops are computable: counter-terms are argued to cancel all divergences.
    • In principle finite $N$ works: products of $N+1$ bulk fields obey constraints excluding even empty AdS.
    • The critical model keeps the action; only the scalar's boundary condition changes.
  • Why it matters No sign of a topology sum appears; high-spin gravity presumably gains a quantum completion.

specialist.html:
• Context Vasiliev's theory has no action. Bi-local holography, notably de Mello Koch–Jevicki–Suzuki–Yoon, proposes building the bulk from $G(x_1,x_2)=\frac1N\sum_I\phi_I^*(x_1)\phi_I(x_2)$.
  • Result
    • Identifying conformal partial-wave coefficients of $G$'s fluctuation $\eta$, up to $f_{\Delta,J}$, with bulk-to-boundary coefficients of transverse traceless $\Phi_J$ gives an invertible map (modified for the $d<4$ scalar), finite if $f$ is a power times a phase at large $s$.
    • If $f_{\Delta,J}f_{d-\Delta,J}=(-1)^J$ the quadratic action is $\Phi_J(\nabla^2-M^2_{d+J-2,J})(\nabla^2-M^2_{d+J,J})\Phi_J$, with Faddeev–Popov-like ghosts for $U(N)$, not $O(N)$; the non-local whole is presumably Vasiliev's, gauge-fixed.
    • Counter-terms $\propto V\sim L^d/\varepsilon^d$ cancel the one-loop tadpole exactly; all loops are argued to cancel.
    • In principle, at finite $N$ the rank bound on $G$ becomes constraints on products of $N+1$ bulk fields, excluding empty AdS.
    • The critical model keeps the action, with $\Pi^{TT}_{d-2,0}\to\Pi^{TT}_{2,0}$ for the scalar.
  • Why it matters No sign of a topology sum, only fields on fixed AdS; high-spin gravity presumably gains an off-shell quantum completion.

brief.html:
Holography defines the bulk through the CFT, but only within the $1/N$ expansion is it understood as fields around a classical solution; beyond it, even whether the bulk is a sum over configurations is open. The paper suggests answers in the simplest example: $N$ free scalars restricted to $U(N)$ or $O(N)$ singlets, dual to high-spin gravity. It rewrites their path integral, explicitly within the $1/N$ expansion, as one over fields of all integer spins on a fixed AdS space, through an invertible map. This gives an explicit, if non-local, action for high-spin gravity, which until now had only equations of motion, and it shows no sign of a sum over topologies.

All singlet information sits in the bi-local field $G(x_1,x_2)=\frac1N\sum_I\phi_I^*(x_1)\phi_I(x_2)$. On a lattice of $V$ points it is a non-negative matrix of rank at most $N$. For $N\ge V$ the rank bound is empty, and changing variables to $G$ only adds the Jacobian term $(N-V)\,\mathrm{Tr}\log G$, which is highly non-local. The whole action is then of order $N$, so expanding $G$ around the free propagator gives Feynman rules in $1/N$, with counter-terms proportional to $V$.

The fluctuation of $G$ is then expanded in eigenmodes of the conformal group: three-point functions with an operator of spin $J$ and dimension $\Delta=\frac d2+is$ on the principal series. Transverse traceless spin-$J$ fields on AdS, expanded in bulk-to-boundary propagators, carry the same labels. So the two sets of coefficients are identified, up to a factor $f_{\Delta,J}$ that conformal symmetry leaves free. The map and its inverse are linear integrals, finite as long as $f_{\Delta,J}$ grows at most like a power along the principal series. On-shell, the boundary limit of each spin-$J$ field gives the corresponding single-trace operator.

Substituted into the quadratic bi-local action, the map gives a non-local bulk kernel. For the choice $f_{\Delta,J}f_{d-\Delta,J}=(-1)^J$ it becomes local but has four derivatives, $\Phi_J(\nabla^2-M^2_{d+J-2,J})(\nabla^2-M^2_{d+J,J})\Phi_J$, where $M^2_{\Delta,J}=\Delta(\Delta-d)-J$. Each spin therefore carries two particles: one of dimension $d-2+J$ with a positive propagator, massless for $J>0$, and one of dimension $d+J$ with a negative propagator. For $U(N)$ the physical particles are exactly Vasiliev's, and the wrong-sign ones have the quantum numbers of the Faddeev–Popov ghosts that gauge-fixing Vasiliev's fields produces. For $O(N)$ the ghosts come out with even spin where Vasiliev's would be odd, a mismatch the paper leaves open. The paper claims its action as the off-shell definition of Vasiliev's theory in this gauge, perturbatively in $1/N$.

The higher terms map to bulk vertices, non-local for any $f$, with the bi-local theory's powers of $N$ and counter-terms. Two diagram identities, inherited from the conformal completeness relation, reduce a bulk loop to a tree diagram times a factor $V$, so the one-loop tadpole cancels its counter-term exactly. Every diagram reduces this way, so the bi-local cancellations should carry over; with radial and infrared cutoffs, divergences appear only through $V\propto L^d/\varepsilon^d$, and they cancel.

The formalism also maps deformations. A mass for the scalars acts only at the boundary of AdS. At leading order it turns on the bulk scalar alone, as a function of $mz$ that breaks the AdS isometries, $\langle\Phi_0\rangle\propto m^2z^2$ for small mass. For a finite mass, a separate map for configurations that do not decay gives the profile numerically in $d=3$. Equivalence with Vasiliev's equations is expected, not shown, and whether the non-local action is local on scales much larger than the AdS radius is open. The construction is for flat $\mathbb R^d$; on spaces with circles, where vector models have phase transitions, it is likely to need modification.

defs.html: Not required to solve the classical equations of motion; a path integral sums over all such configurations. Its opposite, on-shell, here also describes a relation between operators that holds only inside correlation functions. The paper's maps between CFT and bulk variables are off-shell, unlike the usual dictionary.

at.quote: Do off-shell gravitational configurations have any meaning?

defs.html: A theory of $N$ fields $\phi_I$ forming a vector of $U(N)$ (complex) or $O(N)$ (real), here $N$ free scalars, or their critical point, restricted to singlets. Its single-trace operators are bilinears $\phi^*\partial^J\phi$, one primary of each spin, conserved for $J>0$: the simplest example of AdS/CFT.

A gravitational theory in AdS with massless gauge fields of every spin, the graviton among them, conjectured dual to vector models. Classically it is described by Vasiliev's equations of motion, which have a huge gauge symmetry but no known action; the paper's bulk theory is presumably a gauge-fixed form of it.

A definition of a theory beyond its classical limit. Here: an off-shell action for high-spin gravity, which classically has only equations of motion, that fixes its loop corrections in $1/N$. The paper's completion is the one that reproduces the vector model at every order.

The programme, going back to Das and Jevicki's large-$N$ collective fields, of deriving the bulk dual of a vector model by changing variables to the singlet bi-local field $G(x_1,x_2)$. The paper builds on it, and in particular on the recent version of de Mello Koch, Jevicki, Suzuki and Yoon.

The singlet $G(x_1,x_2)=\frac1N\sum_I\phi_I^*(x_1)\phi_I(x_2)$, a product of the scalars at two points. Its correlators hold all singlet information, and local operators of every spin are its Taylor coefficients as $x_2\to x_1$. Its fluctuation around the free propagator, scaled by $\sqrt N$, is called $\eta$.

at.quote: map the bi-local fields to the bulk

defs.html: The relations among components of $G$ that follow from its being a sum of $N$ products: on $V$ lattice points, $G$ and each of its blocks have rank at most $N$. They are absent for $N\ge V$, the regime of the $1/N$ expansion, and unsolved for $N<V$; in the bulk they become constraints on products of $N+1$ fields.

Here, the terms proportional to the cutoff $V$, the number of lattice points, that the Jacobian of the change to bi-local variables adds to the action. They are fixed, not tuned: in perturbation theory they cancel the loop divergences, which come in powers of $V$, both in the bi-local theory and in its bulk image.

The dimensions $\Delta=\frac d2+is$, $s$ real, labelling the representations of the Euclidean conformal group $SO(d+1,1)$ over which functions of two points are expanded, in an integral over $s$. Physical operators, with real dimensions, appear as poles of the coefficients, reached by closing or deforming that contour.

The basis of functions of two points made of conformal three-point functions $\langle\mathcal O_{\Delta_0}(x_1)\mathcal O_{\Delta_0}(x_2)\mathcal O_{\Delta,J}(y)\rangle$, labelled by a spin $J$, a principal-series dimension $\Delta$ and a point $y$. They are the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients of the conformal group; the expansion coefficients of $\eta$ are $C_{\Delta,J}(y)$.

A theory whose correlators are all sums of products of two-point functions, as by Wick's theorem, for a field of arbitrary dimension $\Delta_0$. The free scalar is the case $\Delta_0=(d-2)/2$; the paper works at general $\Delta_0$ to control analytic continuations, then sets that value.

A bookkeeping in which points of $d$-dimensional space are null rays $P$ in $\mathbb R^{d+1,1}$ and AdS$_{d+1}$ is the hyperboloid $X^2=-1$, so that conformal transformations and AdS isometries act linearly. Spin indices are carried by auxiliary null vectors, $Z$ on the boundary and $W$ in the bulk.

The shadow of a dimension $\Delta$ is $\tilde\Delta=d-\Delta$. Representations with $\Delta$ and $\tilde\Delta$ are equivalent, and the shadow transform, an integral against a two-point function, maps one to the other up to a shadow coefficient. On the principal series the shadow is the complex conjugate, so half the modes are redundant.

at.quote: where the shadow coefficient is defined as

defs.html: The spin-$J$ solution $G_{\Delta,J}(X,y)$ of the AdS wave equation that is singular only at one boundary point $y$, where it behaves as if sourced by an operator of dimension $\Delta$. On the principal series these propagators are a complete basis for bulk fields, as three-point functions are for the bi-local field.

Said of a bulk tensor field with vanishing divergence, $\nabla^\mu\Phi_{\mu\mu_2\dots\mu_J}=0$. The paper's bulk fields are symmetric, traceless and transverse, the form a massless high-spin gauge field takes after gauge fixing, so they carry no gauge redundancy.

Said of a field of spin $J\ge1$ with a gauge symmetry, like the photon ($J=1$) and the graviton ($J=2$), so that only its transverse traceless polarizations propagate. In AdS such fields are dual to conserved currents; here they have dimension $d-2+J$ and come from the currents $\phi^*\partial^J\phi$.

Here, the second particle of each spin in the bulk quadratic action, with dimension $d+J$ and a propagator of the wrong sign, which the paper treats as unphysical. For $U(N)$ its quantum numbers match the Faddeev–Popov ghosts of gauge-fixed massless high-spin fields, and the paper uses “ghost” in both senses.

The factor $f_{\Delta,J}$ in $C^{bulk}_{\Delta,J}=f_{\Delta,J}C_{\Delta,J}$, relating CFT and bulk mode coefficients, which conformal symmetry leaves free. Shadow consistency fixes its ratio to its shadow, and the choice $f^{\rm local}$ makes the quadratic action local; bulk diagrams depend on $f$ only through their external legs.

The bulk function $\Omega_{\Delta,J}(X_1,X_2)$: two bulk-to-boundary propagators, of dimensions $\Delta$ and $d-\Delta$, integrated over their common boundary point. It solves the homogeneous wave equation, is proportional to the difference of the propagators with the two boundary conditions, and integrated over the principal series it gives the delta function.

In this paper, the propagator $\Pi_{\Delta,J}$ of a spin-$J$ field with a standard two-derivative kinetic term and mass set by $\Delta$, not the two-point function of the paper's own fields, which are combinations of such propagators. Its transverse part $\Pi^{TT}$ stays finite for massless fields.

Said of a bi-local or bulk configuration that does not vanish far away, such as the expectation value produced by a uniform mass. The conformal basis cannot expand it, so the paper maps such parts separately, by Mellin transforms in $|x_1-x_2|$ and in $z$; they carry no dynamics.

Adding a mass term $m^2\sum_I|\phi_I|^2$ to the free scalars. The theory stays free but is no longer conformal; its bulk dual, at leading order, is AdS with the scalar field turned on, depending only on $mz$ and so breaking the AdS isometries.

at.quote: a mass deformation where we give a mass

defs.html: The interacting conformal field theory reached in the infrared, for $2<d<4$, by adding the quartic interaction $(\sum_I|\phi_I|^2)^2$ to the free scalars: the critical $U(N)$ or $O(N)$ model. At leading order in $1/N$ it is the free theory with $\phi^*\phi$, of dimension $d-2$, replaced by an operator of dimension 2.

at.quote: the critical theory is described by the same bulk action

defs.html: A deformation by the square of a single-trace operator, here $(\phi^*\phi)^2$, proportional to $G(x,x)^2$. At large $N$ it changes only two-point functions at leading order, and in the bulk only the boundary condition of the field dual to $\phi^*\phi$.

An auxiliary field $\sigma(x)$ that turns the quartic interaction into a coupling linear in $\eta(x,x)$; integrating it out gives back $\lambda\eta^2$. In the critical limit $\lambda\to\infty$ it becomes a Lagrange multiplier setting $\eta(x,x)$ to zero, and its correlators are those of the dimension-2 operator.

questions.q: Does the bulk path integral include other geometries or topologies?
questions.a: Not for these models on $\mathbb R^d$. The paper finds only continuous field configurations, metric fluctuations included, on one fixed AdS space, and no sign of a sum over topologies. This is expected to change on spaces with circles, where vector models have large-$N$ phase transitions thought to map to changes of bulk topology; there the construction would need $U(N)$ gauge fields and holonomies, which the paper does not treat.

questions.q: What does the paper not show?
questions.a: It does not prove that loops cancel to all orders, nor that its classical theory is Vasiliev's in some gauge. It does not write the finite-$N$ constraints in bulk terms, or check that the action is local at distances much larger than the AdS radius. It treats only Euclidean $\mathbb R^d$, so backgrounds with circles, Lorentzian signature, fermions and matrix models are left open, as is the $O(N)$ ghost mismatch.

questions.q: What do $N$, $V$, $d$, $\Delta_0$, $\Delta$ and $J$ stand for, and in which order are the limits taken?
questions.a: $N$ counts the scalars and $d>2$ is the boundary dimension, so the bulk is AdS$_{d+1}$. $V$ is the number of lattice points of the regularized theory, standing for UV and IR cutoffs. $\Delta_0=(d-2)/2$ is the free scalar's dimension, and $\Delta$, $J$ label conformal modes and bulk fields, with $\Delta=\frac d2+is$ on the principal series. The $1/N$ expansion takes $N\to\infty$ first, so $N\ge V$, and removes the cutoff afterwards; finite $N$ in the continuum means $N<V$.

Then $N<V$, and $G$ has rank at most $N$, which relates products of $N+1$ of its components. A path integral over the allowed $G$ still exists, but its explicit form is not known. Mapped to the bulk, the relations become non-local constraints on products of bulk fields, which exclude most configurations, empty AdS among them. The paper expects the passage from $N\ge V$ to $N<V$ to be smooth but does not show it.

questions.q: Why must loop corrections cancel, and is this proven?
questions.a: In the free theory every connected correlator of $\sqrt N\eta$ comes from a single loop of scalar propagators and is exactly proportional to $N$, so in the $1/N$ expansion every loop correction must vanish, with the counter-terms supplying the cancellation. The paper verifies this at one loop, in the bi-local theory and in the bulk, and reduces every diagram to powers of $V$ times a tree, but gives no explicit all-orders proof; it follows implicitly from the exact change of variables.

The coefficients $C_{\Delta,J}$ are defined by an integral that converges only for $\Delta_0>d/4$, that is $d>4$ for free fields. For $2<d<4$ the paper expands the double shadow of $\eta$ instead and deforms the $J=0$ contour to include $\Delta=d-2$ and exclude its shadow 2, which turns the scalar maps into differential operators. At $d=4$ the change of variables breaks down, and results are continued from $d>4$. In $d=2$ the free propagator is a logarithm and that case is not considered.

questions.q: Is the map from the CFT to the bulk unique?
questions.a: No. Conformal symmetry fixes it only up to a factor $f_{\Delta,J}$ for each mode. Consistency with the shadow relation fixes the ratio $f_{\Delta,J}/f_{d-\Delta,J}$, reality fixes its phase, and finiteness needs $|f|$ to grow at most like a power along the principal series. The rest is a choice of bulk field variables: one choice makes the quadratic action local, and bulk diagrams depend on $f$ only through their external legs.

questions.q: How does this map differ from the usual reconstruction of bulk fields?
questions.a: HKLL-type reconstruction writes on-shell bulk fields as smeared local CFT operators. This map is off-shell and exact: it sends the bi-local field, a variable of the CFT path integral, to bulk field configurations, so it maps one path integral to another, actions included. Only in the boundary limit, and on-shell, does it reduce to the familiar dictionary between $\Phi_J$ and the spin-$J$ single-trace operator.

Only in part. With the special normalization $f^{\rm local}$ the quadratic action is local, but it has four derivatives, which is why each spin carries two particles. The cubic and higher vertices are non-local for any choice of $f$. On general grounds the dual of a free theory is not expected to be local below the AdS radius, but it should be at much longer distances; whether this action has that property is left open.

questions.q: Is this theory Vasiliev's high-spin gravity?
questions.a: The paper believes so but does not show it. For $U(N)$ the physical spectrum matches Vasiliev's, and Vasiliev's equations can be written on a fixed AdS background, as here. The paper expects a specific gauge fixing to reduce them to its action's classical equations, which would make the action the off-shell, loop-level definition of Vasiliev's theory. Its quadratic terms differ from the naive ones of Vasiliev's fields, and for $O(N)$ the ghost spins disagree.

questions.q: Are the wrong-sign particles a problem?
questions.a: They are interpreted as unphysical. For $U(N)$ their spins and masses are those of the Faddeev–Popov ghosts of massless high-spin fields in a transverse traceless gauge, and they are subleading when a point goes to the boundary, so they do not affect CFT correlators. For $O(N)$ their spins disagree with those of Vasiliev's ghosts, which the paper cannot explain. Their role in a Lorentzian bulk Hilbert space is listed as an open question.

questions.q: Where does the cutoff $V$ come from in the bulk?
questions.a: In the bi-local theory $V={\rm Tr}\,1$ is the number of lattice points; it enters the Jacobian and hence the counter-terms. In the bulk the same factor appears when a loop closes the completeness relation onto itself, giving $\int dP\,\delta(0)$. A radial cutoff $z>\varepsilon$ and a cutoff $|x|<L$ regularize it to $V\sim L^d/\varepsilon^d$, provided the sum over internal spins is done before the cutoffs are removed.

questions.q: What bulk configuration does the mass deformation give?
questions.a: The space stays AdS; at leading order in $1/N$ only the bulk scalar acquires an expectation value, which depends on $z$ through $mz$ alone and so breaks the AdS isometries. For small mass it is proportional to $m^2z^2$, the fall-off of the shadow of the mass operator. For finite mass in $d=3$ it is a contour integral evaluated numerically; the paper suggests comparing it with mass-deformed solutions of Vasiliev's equations.

questions.q: Why does the critical model differ from the free one only by a boundary condition?
questions.a: At large $N$ the double-trace interaction changes only the two-point function of $\eta(x,x)$, which for $d<4$ is, off-shell, the boundary limit of the bulk scalar. In the bulk this replaces the physical scalar propagator $\Pi^{TT}_{d-2,0}$ by $\Pi^{TT}_{2,0}$, which solves the same equation with the other fall-off. Since the difference has no short-distance singularities, an argument of Giombi and Yin then gives the critical correlators at all orders, with the action unchanged.
